CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: [Category: Loss Function]
- What: In model_design, replace independent binary logistic loss with sampled-softmax cross-entropy over each positive and its existing 64 uniform negative samples. Compute loss as logsumexp of the positive and valid negative logits minus the positive logit, masking history items and target collisions out of the denominator; retain equal weighting across examples.
- Why: HR@10 measures relative candidate ranking, whereas the current loss independently pushes positive and negative scores toward absolute classification targets; sampled softmax directly makes the observed next item compete against alternatives.

---

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: Averaging independent negative losses can dilute the influence of difficult competing items, potentially spending updates on already well-separated negatives.
- Evidence: The current model achieves macro HR@10=0.4775 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.505, with Electronics falling from 0.420 to 0.305; these results justify testing the objective but do not establish it as the cause because the architectures also differ.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: Sampled-softmax gradients emphasize negatives with larger scores, concentrating learning on ordering errors most relevant to candidate ranking while updating the same single network.
- Expected improvement: The experimental hypothesis is an absolute macro HR@10 gain of 0.01–0.03 over 0.4775, with the host’s pinned validation determining whether the change succeeds.
- Synergy (if multiple changes): Not applicable; change only the training objective and its descriptive logging.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: Preprocessing seed=0; training and evaluation seeds=42.
- Data split: Identical supplied training and validation splits; validation labels remain excluded from gradient updates, and hidden test files remain unread.
- Model: Current HistoryModel architecture, tied item embeddings, jointly trained item bias, pooling, dropout, dimensions, and scoring formula.
- Training: Prefix sampling, 64 uniform negatives, collision masking, batch size, optimizer, learning-rate policy, gradient clipping, epoch limit, and checkpoint selection remain identical to the previous code.
- Evaluation: Macro-average HR@10 across all four categories, using the pinned host evaluator with 200 validation users per category and 99 unique negative candidates.
- Inference: One independently trained model and one selected checkpoint per category; preserve all four dataset routes and identical validation/predictor scoring, without averaging or auxiliary predictors.
- Artifacts: DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save checkpoints and working/predict.py beneath the trial directory, with test inference performed by the host.
